meta_description:
7,308 likes, 160 comments - labourlawadvisor on October 6, 2026: "Comment ‘UPI’ and we will send you complete e-rupee guide!

Want to pay digitally without a UPI fee on the shop’s side? The RBI already has something for that.

It is called the Digital Rupee, or e₹, and the RBI calls it “Cash but Digital.” It is the digital form of the rupee, issued by the RBI itself, so it carries the same guarantee as the notes in your pocket and counts as legal tender. You keep it in an e₹ wallet on your phone and use it just like cash. You can pay a friend or a shopkeeper by scanning a CBDC QR code. You can even scan a UPI QR from the e₹ app, though in that case settlement follows UPI timelines.

Here is what makes it interesting for everyday use:

No charges or fees for using e₹ or the wallet.
No minimum balance needed.
You can load money from your bank account or redeem it back 24x7.
It works on both Android and iOS.
If your phone is lost, your e₹ stays safe and you can recover the wallet on a new phone using the same number or SIM.
Need to pay ₹15 with a ₹20 note in your wallet? The wallet automatically sends ₹15 and keeps the ₹5 change.

One thing to know before you rush to download it. e₹ is still being piloted, and wallets are currently offered by 19 banks, including SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bank of Baroda, PNB and Canara Bank. Your wallet is linked to your savings account, and no interest is paid on the balance, because it works like physical cash. The RBI is also working on an offline feature for places with weak internet.

Save this post so you can find the list of banks later, watch the video till the end, and share it with someone who still carries cash everywhere.

#DigitalRupee #eRupee #CBDC #RBI".
